morgan: Customer reports intermittent 401s coming through their edge proxy, but they have no request id visible in the Redwood Console. They say requests originate from a mobile webview and the errors happened around 2026-03-15T17:04:00Z. Any quick repro capture advice?

alex: First ask whether calls are server->server or embedded browser. For proxies it's very common to strip/overwrite correlation headers. Ask for: exact UTC timestamps, endpoint path, and the user-agent string. Also ask if they can run a curl or spin a short-lived API key to let us search logs.

samir: Two pragmatic captures we use: 1) curl from inside the same network/proxy to inject a recognizable header, 2) HAR or remote debugging capture for webviews. Example curl (replace host/key):

````
curl -i 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TEMP_KEY>' \
  -H 'X-Redwood-Debug: acme-xyz-890' \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
````

Request them to paste the full verbose output (-v/-i) so we can see request and response headers. If our logs show X-Redwood-Debug=acme-xyz-890 then we can correlate the exact server request.

jessica: If they can't run curl, HAR steps for embedded browser: open DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right click -> Save all as HAR with content. For mobile webview: Android -> chrome://inspect remote device; iOS -> Safari Web Inspector connected to device. If device attach isn't possible, ask them to proxy traffic through Charles/Fiddler and export a session. Include the approximate UTC timestamp for each failing call (minute granularity ok).

samir: Additional helpful fields: client IP (if known), request path, full request/response headers, body snippet, and any proxy rules (e.g., header whitelist/strip). If they can provide the edge config snippet that shows header handling, that helps a lot.

alex: If they prefer not to share long-lived keys, the short-lived key trick works: ask them to create a key for 5–10 minutes, call the endpoint behind the proxy, then revoke the key. We can then grep server logs for that key. Also ask them to rotate it afterwards per security best practices.

morgan: On the Console side, searching tips: open Console -> Requests -> filter by time window -> search for any string in the header or body (we do case-insensitive substring matches). If they supplied a custom X- header we don't ingest, it may still appear in the raw request detail. If nothing shows, we try matching by proxied IP + timestamp + user-agent.

jessica: For SDK users: ask them to raise log level to debug and capture SDK logs which usually include our internal request id fields (e.g., request_id or redwood_request in Node/Python clients). Provide SDK snippet examples if needed.

samir: Example Node SDK debug snippet to print headers:

````
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.TEMP_KEY });
client.on('request', (req) => console.log('OUTGOING', req.headers, req.path));
````

morgan: I'll send ACME the curl + HAR instructions, the short-lived key suggestion, and a checklist: UTC timestamps, endpoint, user-agent, proxy rules, HAR/curl output, and optional short-lived key. I'll ask them to mark any PII before sending.

support-bot: Runbook attached: /internal/runbooks/edge-proxy-correlation. Follow escalation flow if we cannot correlate in < 2 hours: include timestamps, any candidate IPs, and the short-lived key if used.

morgan: Thanks — will update thread when they respond with artifacts. If they only provide a 401 body with no id, escalate to eng-runtime with the full delta (timestamps + any IPs + client headers).
